chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who cut off one of a woman's fingers—how much is due for it? He said: “Ten camels.” I said: If he cut off two? He said: “Twenty camels.” I said: If he cut off three? He said: “Thirty camels.” He said: I said: Four? He said: “Twenty camels.”

I said: Glory be to Allah! He cuts off three, so thirty are due from him, and he cuts off four, so twenty are due from him! This used to reach us while we were in Iraq, and we would dissociate ourselves from whoever said it, and we would say: the one who brought it was a devil.

So he said: “Take it easy, O Aban. This is the ruling of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. A woman is equal to a man in blood-compensation up to one-third of the diyah; then when it reaches one-third, she returns to one-half. O Aban, you approached me through analogy, and when the sunnah (prophetic tradition) is subjected to analogy, the religion is effaced.”

key_terms.إِصْبَعًا: a finger, the injured body part discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الثُّلُثَ: one-third, the threshold mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood-compensation paid for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.النِّصْفِ: one-half, the reduced proportion after the threshold is reached
key_terms.الْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit in which blood-compensation is measured here
key_terms.الْقِيَاسِ: analogy, which is rejected here when opposed to the sunnah (prophetic tradition)
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, from whom the ruling is traced

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on diyah for a woman’s fingers, and what does this hadith say about qiyas?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on compensation for injuries to a woman’s fingers and explains that her diyah matches that of a man up to one-third of the full blood-compensation, after which it returns to one-half. It also strongly rejects qiyas in the face of the transmitted sunnah (prophetic tradition), presenting the ruling as the judgment of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
